sanskrit: tataḥ śūrpaṇakhā dīnā rāvaṇaṃ lokarāvaṇam amātyamadhye saṃkruddhā paruṣaṃ vākyam abravīt
english: Then Śūrpaṇakhā, wretched and enraged, spoke harsh words to Rāvaṇa, the terror of the world, in the midst of his ministers.

sanskrit: pramattaḥ kāmabhogeṣu svairavṛtto niraṅkuśaḥ samutpannaṃ bhayaṃ ghoraṃ boddhavyaṃ nāvabudhyase
english: "You are intoxicated with sensual pleasures, wandering at will, unchecked — you do not perceive the terrible danger that has arisen, which ought to be understood."

sanskrit: saktaṃ grāmyeṣu bhogeṣu kāmavṛttaṃ mahīpatim lubdhaṃ na bahu manyante śmaśānāgnim iva prajāḥ
english: "A lord of the earth who is addicted to vulgar pleasures, ruled by desire, and greedy — his subjects do not hold him in esteem, just as they regard a cremation-ground fire."

sanskrit: svayaṃ kāryāṇi yaḥ kāle nānutiṣṭhati pārthivaḥ sa tu vai saha rājyena taiś ca kāryair vinaśyati
english: "A king who does not himself attend to affairs at the proper time perishes together with his kingdom and those very affairs."

sanskrit: ayuktacāraṃ durdarśam asvādhīnaṃ narādhipam varjayanti narā dūrān nadīpaṅkam iva dvipāḥ
english: "Men shun from afar a lord of men who has no proper intelligence-network, who is hard to approach, and who has lost self-mastery — as elephants shun the mire of a river."

sanskrit: ye na rakṣanti viṣayam asvādhīnā narādhipaḥ te na vṛddhyā prakāśante girayaḥ sāgare yathā
english: "Those lords of men who have lost self-mastery and do not protect their realm do not shine with prosperity, just as mountains do not shine within the ocean."

sanskrit: ātmavadbhir vigṛhya tvaṃ devagandharvadānavaiḥ ayuktacāraś capalaḥ kathaṃ rājā bhaviṣyasi
english: "Having made enemies of those with composure — gods, gandharvas, and dānavas — lacking intelligence-service and being fickle, how will you remain a king?"

sanskrit: yeṣāṃ cāraś ca kośaś ca nayaś ca jayatāṃ vara asvādhīnā narendrāṇāṃ prākṛtais te janaiḥ samāḥ
english: "O best among conquerors, those lords of men whose intelligence-network, treasury, and statecraft are not under their own control are equal to common people."

sanskrit: yasmāt paśyanti dūrasthān sarvān arthān narādhipāḥ cāreṇa tasmād ucyante rājāno dīrghacakṣuṣaḥ
english: "Because lords of men see through their spies all matters even from afar, kings are therefore called 'those of far-reaching sight.'"

sanskrit: ayuktacāraṃ manye tvāṃ prākṛtaiḥ sacivair vṛtam svajanaṃ ca janasthānaṃ hataṃ yo nāvabudhyase
english: "I consider you to be without proper intelligence-service, surrounded by ordinary ministers — for you did not perceive the slaughter of your own people in Janasthāna."

sanskrit: caturdaśa sahasrāṇi rakṣasāṃ bhīmakarmaṇām hatāny ekena rāmeṇa kharaś ca sahadūṣaṇaḥ
english: "Fourteen thousand rākṣasas of terrible deeds have been slain by Rāma alone, and Khara together with Dūṣaṇa as well."

sanskrit: ṛṣīṇām abhayaṃ dattaṃ kṛtakṣemāś ca daṇḍakāḥ dharṣitaṃ ca janasthānaṃ rāmeṇākliṣṭakarmaṇā
english: "Safety has been granted to the sages, the Daṇḍaka forest has been made secure, and Janasthāna has been overrun by Rāma, whose deeds are effortless."

sanskrit: tvaṃ tu lubdhaḥ pramattaś ca parādhīnaś ca rāvaṇa viṣaye sve samutpannaṃ bhayaṃ yo nāvabudhyase
english: "But you, Rāvaṇa, are greedy, heedless, and dependent on others — you who do not perceive the danger that has arisen in your own domain."

sanskrit: tīkṣṇam alpapradātāraṃ pramattaṃ garvitaṃ śaṭham vyasane sarvabhūtāni nābhidhāvanti pārthivam
english: "All creatures do not rush to the aid of a king in misfortune who is harsh, gives little, is heedless, arrogant, and deceitful."

sanskrit: atimāninam agrāhyam ātmasaṃbhāvitaṃ naram krodhanaṃ vyasane hanti svajano 'pi narādhipam
english: "Even his own people slay a lord of men in his misfortune who is excessively proud, unapproachable, self-conceited, and irascible."

sanskrit: nānutiṣṭhati kāryāṇi bhayeṣu na bibheti ca kṣipraṃ rājyāc cyuto dīnas tṛṇais tulyo bhaviṣyati
english: "He who does not attend to affairs and does not fear dangers will swiftly be cast from his kingdom and become wretched, equal to a blade of grass."

sanskrit: śuṣkakāṣṭhair bhavet kāryaṃ loṣṭair api ca pāṃsubhiḥ na tu sthānāt paribhraṣṭaiḥ kāryaṃ syād vasudhādhipaiḥ
english: "One may find use in dry wood, in clods of earth, even in dust — but there is no use in lords of the earth who have fallen from their station."

sanskrit: upabhuktaṃ yathā vāsaḥ srajo vā mṛditā yathā evaṃ rājyāt paribhraṣṭaḥ samartho 'pi nirarthakaḥ
english: "Just as a garment already worn, or a garland already crushed, so one fallen from kingship is without value even if capable."

sanskrit: apramattaś ca yo rājā sarvajño vijitendriyaḥ kṛtajño dharmaśīlaś ca sa rājā tiṣṭhate ciram
english: "A king who is vigilant, omniscient, who has conquered his senses, is grateful, and is devoted to righteousness — such a king endures long."

sanskrit: nayanābhyāṃ prasupto 'pi jāgarti nayacakṣuṣā vyaktakrodhaprasādaś ca sa rājā pūjyate janaiḥ
english: "Though asleep with his eyes, he is awake with the eye of statecraft; and whose anger and favor are clearly manifest — such a king is honored by the people."

sanskrit: tvaṃ tu rāvaṇadurbuddhir guṇair etair vivarjitaḥ yasya te 'viditaś cārai rakṣasāṃ sumahān vadhaḥ
english: "But you, Rāvaṇa of wicked intellect, are devoid of these virtues — you by whose spies the great slaughter of your rākṣasas was not made known to you."

sanskrit: parāvamantā viṣayeṣu saṃgato nadeśa kālapravibhāga tattvavit ayuktabuddhir guṇadoṣaniścaye vipannarājyo na cirād vipatsyate
english: "One who despises others, addicted to sense-pleasures, ignorant of the true nature of distinctions of place and time, of disordered intellect in judging merits and faults — such a ruined king will soon come to total destruction."

sanskrit: iti svadoṣān parikīrtitāṃs tayā samīkṣya buddhyā kṣaṇadācareśvaraḥ dhanena darpeṇa balena cānvito vicintayām āsa ciraṃ sa rāvaṇaḥ
english: Thus having considered with his intellect those own faults enumerated by her, Rāvaṇa — the lord of those who move in the night, endowed with wealth, pride, and power — reflected for a long while.

sanskrit: tataḥ śūrpaṇakhāṃ kruddhāṃ bruvatīṃ paruṣaṃ vacaḥ amātyamadhye saṃkruddhaḥ paripapraccha rāvaṇaḥ
english: Then Rāvaṇa, himself aroused to anger, questioned Śūrpaṇakhā who was speaking harsh words in anger, in the midst of his ministers.

sanskrit: kaś ca rāmaḥ kathaṃ vīryaḥ kiṃ rūpaḥ kiṃ parākramaḥ kimarthaṃ daṇḍakāraṇyaṃ praviṣṭaś ca suduścaram
english: "Who is this Rāma? What is his valor? What is his form, and what his prowess? And for what reason has he entered the Daṇḍaka forest, which is so very hard to penetrate?"

sanskrit: āyudhaṃ kiṃ ca rāmasya nihatā yena rākṣasāḥ kharaś ca nihataṃ saṃkhye dūṣaṇas triśirās tathā
english: "What is Rāma's weapon, with which the rākṣasas were slain, and Khara was killed in battle along with Dūṣaṇa and Triśiras?"

sanskrit: ity uktā rākṣasendreṇa rākṣasī krodhamūrchitā tato rāmaṃ yathānyāyam ākhyātum upacakrame
english: Thus addressed by the lord of rākṣasas, the rākṣasī, overcome with rage, then began to describe Rāma in proper order.

sanskrit: dīrghabāhur viśālākṣaś cīrakṛṣṇājināmbaraḥ kandarpasamarūpaś ca rāmo daśarathātmajaḥ
english: "Rāma, son of Daśaratha, is long-armed, broad-eyed, clad in barkcloth and black antelope skin, and equal in beauty to the god of love."

sanskrit: śakracāpanibhaṃ cāpaṃ vikṛṣya kanakāṅgadam dīptān kṣipati nārācān sarpān iva mahāviṣān
english: "Drawing his bow that resembles Indra's rainbow, with his golden armlets, he releases blazing iron arrows like mighty venomous serpents."

sanskrit: nādadānaṃ śarān ghorān na muñcantaṃ mahābalam na kārmukaṃ vikarṣantaṃ rāmaṃ paśyāmi saṃyuge
english: "In the battle I could not see Rāma, that great warrior, taking up his terrible arrows, releasing them, or drawing his bow — so swift was he."

sanskrit: hanyamānaṃ tu tat sainyaṃ paśyāmi śaravṛṣṭibhiḥ indreṇaivottamaṃ sasyaṃ āhataṃ tv aśmavṛṣṭibhiḥ
english: "Yet I saw that army being slain by showers of arrows, as the finest crop is struck down by Indra's hailstorms."

sanskrit: rakṣasāṃ bhīmavīryāṇāṃ sahasrāṇi caturdaśa nihatāni śarais tīkṣṇais tenaikena padātinā
english: "Fourteen thousand rākṣasas of terrible valor have been slain by sharp arrows by that one man fighting on foot."

sanskrit: ardhādhikamuhūrtena kharaś ca sahadūṣaṇaḥ ṛṣīṇām abhayaṃ dattaṃ kṛtakṣemāś ca daṇḍakāḥ
english: "In somewhat more than half a muhūrta, Khara together with Dūṣaṇa was slain; safety was granted to the sages, and the Daṇḍaka forest was made secure."

sanskrit: ekā kathaṃ cin muktāhaṃ paribhūya mahātmanā strīvadhaṃ śaṅkamānena rāmeṇa viditātmanā
english: "I alone escaped somehow, scorned by that great-souled Rāma, that knower of the self, who was reluctant to slay a woman."

sanskrit: bhrātā cāsya mahātejā guṇatas tulyavikramaḥ anuraktaś ca bhaktaś ca lakṣmaṇo nāma vīryavān
english: "His brother too is of great splendor, equal in valor by virtue of his qualities, devoted and loyal — the mighty one named Lakṣmaṇa."

sanskrit: amarṣī durjayo jetā vikrānto buddhimān balī rāmasya dakṣiṇe bāhur nityaṃ prāṇo bahiṣcaraḥ
english: "Intolerant of insult, unconquerable, a victor, valiant, wise, and powerful — he is the right arm of Rāma, always like his life-breath moving outside him."

sanskrit: rāmasya tu viśālākṣī dharmapatnī yaśasvinī sītā nāma varārohā vaidehī tanumadhyamā
english: "Rāma's lawful wife is the renowned Vaidehī, named Sītā, broad-eyed, of excellent hips, slender-waisted."

sanskrit: naiva devī na gandharvā na yakṣī na ca kiṃnarī tathārūpā mayā nārī dṛṣṭapūrvā mahītale
english: "Neither goddess, nor gandharvī, nor yakṣī, nor kiṃnarī — no woman of such beauty have I ever seen before on this earth."

sanskrit: yasya sītā bhaved bhāryā yaṃ ca hṛṣṭā pariṣvajet atijīvet sa sarveṣu lokeṣv api puraṃdarāt
english: "He whose wife Sītā might be, whom she might joyfully embrace — that one would surpass even Indra the destroyer of citadels in all the worlds."

sanskrit: sā suśīlā vapuḥślāghyā rūpeṇāpratimā bhuvi tavānurūpā bhāryā sā tvaṃ ca tasyās tathā patiḥ
english: "She is of good character, praiseworthy of form, without peer in beauty on earth — she is the fitting wife for you, and you would be the fitting husband for her."

sanskrit: tāṃ tu vistīrṇajaghanāṃ pīnottuṅgapayodharām bhāryārthe tu tavānetum udyatāhaṃ varānanām
english: "Her of the broad hips and full, high breasts, of lovely face — I set out to bring her to you for your wife."

sanskrit: tāṃ tu dṛṣṭvādya vaidehīṃ pūrṇacandranibhānanām manmathasya śarāṇāṃ ca tvaṃ vidheyo bhaviṣyasi
english: "When you behold that Vaidehī today, whose face is like the full moon, you will fall under the command of the arrows of Manmatha, the god of love."

sanskrit: yadi tasyām abhiprāyo bhāryārthe tava jāyate śīghram uddhriyatāṃ pādo jayārtham iha dakṣiṇaḥ
english: "If the desire for her as your wife arises in you, then quickly raise your right foot here for the march to victory."

sanskrit: kuru priyaṃ tathā teṣāṃ rakṣasāṃ rākṣaseśvara vadhāt tasya nṛśaṃsasya rāmasyāśramavāsinaḥ
english: "Do what is dear to those rākṣasas likewise, O lord of rākṣasas, by slaying that cruel Rāma who dwells in the hermitage."

sanskrit: taṃ śarair niśitair hatvā lakṣmaṇaṃ ca mahāratham hatanāthāṃ sukhaṃ sītāṃ yathāvad upabhokṣyase
english: "Having slain him with sharp arrows, and Lakṣmaṇa the great chariot-warrior, you will enjoy Sītā, deprived of her lord, easily and as you please."

sanskrit: rocate yadi te vākyaṃ mamaitad rākṣaseśvara kriyatāṃ nirviśaṅkena vacanaṃ mama rāghava
english: "If this my speech pleases you, O lord of rākṣasas, then let my words be carried out without hesitation, O Rāghava."

sanskrit: niśamya rāmeṇa śarair ajihmagair hatāñ janasthānagatān niśācarān kharaṃ ca buddhvā nihataṃ ca dūṣaṇaṃ tvam adya kṛtyaṃ pratipattum arhasi
english: "Having heard of the night-wanderers stationed in Janasthāna slain by Rāma's straight-flying arrows, and knowing that Khara and Dūṣaṇa have been killed, you ought today to undertake the proper course of action."

sanskrit: tataḥ śūrpaṇakhā vākyaṃ tac chrutvā romaharṣaṇam sacivān abhyanujñāya kāryaṃ buddhvā jagāma ha
english: Then Śūrpaṇakhā, having heard that hair-raising speech, took leave of the ministers, and having determined upon her course of action, departed.

sanskrit: tat kāryam anugamyātha yathāvad upalabhya ca doṣāṇāṃ ca guṇānāṃ ca saṃpradhārya balābalam
english: And having pursued that matter, having properly comprehended it, and having weighed the strengths and weaknesses of faults and merits,

sanskrit: iti kartavyam ity eva kṛtvā niścayam ātmanaḥ sthirabuddhis tato ramyāṃ yānaśālāṃ jagāma ha
english: Having thus made his own firm resolve — "this is what must be done" — he, of steadfast mind, then went to the charming vehicle-hall.

sanskrit: yānaśālāṃ tato gatvā pracchannaṃ rākṣasādhipaḥ sūtaṃ saṃcodayām āsa rathaḥ saṃyujyatām iti
english: Having gone to the vehicle-hall, the lord of rākṣasas then secretly commanded the charioteer: "Let the chariot be yoked."

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ kṣaṇenaiva sārathir laghuvikramaḥ rathaṃ saṃyojayām āsa tasyābhimatam uttamam
english: Thus commanded, the charioteer of swift movements yoked in an instant that excellent chariot which was his master's favorite.

sanskrit: kāñcanaṃ ratham āsthāya kāmagaṃ ratnabhūṣitam piśācavadanair yuktaṃ kharaiḥ kanakabhūṣaṇaiḥ
english: Mounting the golden chariot that could go wherever desired, adorned with jewels, yoked with mules of piśāca-faces, ornamented with gold,

sanskrit: meghapratimanādena sa tena dhanadānujaḥ rākṣasādhipatiḥ śrīmān yayau nadanadīpatim
english: With a roar resembling that of a thundercloud, the glorious lord of rākṣasas, younger brother of Kubera the lord of wealth, set forth to the lord of rivers and streams — the ocean.

sanskrit: sa śvetabālavyasanaḥ śvetacchatro daśānanaḥ snigdhavaidūryasaṃkāśas taptakāñcanabhūṣaṇaḥ
english: He with the white fly-whisk and white parasol, the ten-faced one, gleaming like polished vaidūrya gemstone, adorned with refined gold ornaments —

sanskrit: daśāsyo viṃśatibhujo darśanīya paricchadaḥ tridaśārir munīndraghno daśaśīrṣa ivādrirāṭ
english: Ten-mouthed, twenty-armed, of magnificent attire, enemy of the gods, slayer of the lords of sages — like the king of mountains himself with ten peaks.

sanskrit: kāmagaṃ ratham āsthāya śuśubhe rākṣasādhipaḥ vidyunmaṇḍalavān meghaḥ sabalāka ivāmbare
english: Mounted on his wish-moving chariot, the lord of rākṣasas shone resplendent like a cloud wreathed with lightning, accompanied by cranes in the sky.

sanskrit: saśailaṃ sāgarānūpaṃ vīryavān avalokayan nānāpuṣpaphalair vṛkṣair anukīrṇaṃ sahasraśaḥ
english: The mighty one gazed upon the landscape with its mountains and ocean shores, strewn with thousands of trees bearing manifold flowers and fruits,

sanskrit: śītamaṅgalatoyābhiḥ padminībhiḥ samantataḥ viśālair āśramapadair vedimadbhiḥ samāvṛtam
english: Surrounded on all sides by lotus-pools with cool and auspicious waters, covered with vast hermitage sites possessing sacrificial altars,

sanskrit: kadaly āḍhakisaṃbādhaṃ nālikeropaśobhitam sālais tālais tamālaiś ca tarubhiś ca supuṣpitaiḥ
english: Thronged with plantain and āḍhakī plants, adorned with coconut palms, with śāla, palm, tamāla and other trees in full bloom,

sanskrit: atyantaniyatāhāraiḥ śobhitaṃ paramarṣibhiḥ nāgaiś suparṇair gandharvaiḥ kiṃnaraiś ca sahasraśaḥ
english: Beautified by great sages of most rigorously regulated diet, and by thousands of nāgas, suparṇas, gandharvas, and kiṃnaras,

sanskrit: jitakāmaiś ca siddhaiś ca cāmaṇaiś copaśobhitam ājair vaikhānasair māṣair vālakhilyair marīcipaiḥ
english: Adorned with siddhas who have conquered desire, and with cāmaṇas, Ājas, Vaikhānasas, Māṣas, Vālakhilyas, and Marīcipas,

sanskrit: divyābharaṇamālyābhir divyarūpābhir āvṛtam krīḍā ratividhijñābhir apsarobhiḥ sahasraśaḥ
english: Enveloped by thousands of apsarases bearing divine ornaments and garlands, of divine beauty, versed in the arts of sport and love,

sanskrit: sevitaṃ devapatnībhiḥ śrīmatībhiḥ śriyā vṛtam devadānavasaṃghaiś ca caritaṃ tv amṛtāśibhiḥ
english: Frequented by the radiant wives of gods, invested with beauty, and traversed by throngs of gods and dānavas who subsist on ambrosia,

sanskrit: haṃsakrauñcaplavākīrṇaṃ sārasaiḥ saṃpraṇāditam vaidūryaprastaraṃ ramyaṃ snigdhaṃ sāgaratejasā
english: Filled with haṃsas, krauñcas, and plavas, resounding with the calls of sārasas, its vaidūrya-gem floor charming and gleaming with the ocean's luminosity,

sanskrit: pāṇḍurāṇi viśālāni divyamālyayutāni ca tūryagītābhijuṣṭāni vimānāni samantataḥ
english: White and vast celestial vehicles adorned with divine garlands, resounding with musical instruments and song, on every side —

sanskrit: tapasā jitalokānāṃ kāmagāny abhisaṃpatan gandharvāpsarasaś caiva dadarśa dhanadānujaḥ
english: Wish-moving vehicles of those who had won worlds through austerities, flying about — thus did the younger brother of Kubera behold gandharvas and apsarases.

sanskrit: niryāsarasamūlānāṃ candanānāṃ sahasraśaḥ vanāni paśyan saumyāni ghrāṇatṛptikarāṇi ca
english: He saw thousands of gentle, fragrance-satisfying sandalwood groves with their resinous sap at their roots,

sanskrit: agarūṇāṃ ca mukhyānāṃ vanāny upavanāni ca takkolānāṃ ca jātyānāṃ phalānāṃ ca sugandhinām
english: And forests and garden-groves of the finest agaru trees, and of takkola, jātī, and fragrant fruit trees,

sanskrit: puṣpāṇi ca tamālasya gulmāni maricasya ca muktānāṃ ca samūhāni śuṣyamāṇāni tīrataḥ
english: And flowers of the tamāla tree, thickets of pepper plants, and heaps of pearls drying along the shore,

sanskrit: śaṅkhānāṃ prastaraṃ caiva pravālanicayaṃ tathā kāñcanāni ca śailāni rājatāni ca sarvaśaḥ
english: And beds of conch-shells and heaps of coral, and mountains of gold and silver everywhere,

sanskrit: prasravāṇi manojñāni prasannāni hradāni ca dhanadhānyopapannāni strīratnair āvṛtāni ca
english: And charming springs and pellucid lakes endowed with treasure and grain, surrounded by gem-like women,

sanskrit: hastyaśvarathagāḍhāni nagarāṇy avalokayan taṃ samaṃ sarvataḥ snigdhaṃ mṛdusaṃsparśamārutam
english: He looked upon cities dense with elephants, horses, and chariots, and that even, uniformly pleasant land with its gentle-to-the-touch breezes,

sanskrit: anūpaṃ sindhurājasya dadarśa tridivopamam tatrāpaśyat sa meghābhaṃ nyagrodham ṛṣibhir vṛtam
english: He saw the riverine land of the lord of rivers, resembling heaven. There he beheld a cloud-like banyan tree surrounded by sages.

sanskrit: samantād yasya tāḥ śākhāḥ śatayojanam āyatāḥ yasya hastinam ādāya mahākāyaṃ ca kaccapam bhakṣārthaṃ garuḍaḥ śākhām ājagāma mahābalaḥ
english: That tree whose branches extended a hundred yojanas in all directions — to one of whose branches the mighty Garuḍa came, carrying an elephant and a great-bodied tortoise for his meal.

sanskrit: tasya tāṃ sahasā śākhāṃ bhāreṇa patagottamaḥ suparṇaḥ parṇabahulāṃ babhañjātha mahābalaḥ
english: That best of birds, the mighty Suparṇa, suddenly broke that leafy branch of it with the weight, the great-powered one.

sanskrit: tatra vaikhānasā māṣā vālakhilyā marīcipāḥ ajā babhūvur dhūmrāś ca saṃgatāḥ paramarṣayaḥ
english: There were assembled Vaikhānasas, Māṣas, Vālakhilyas, Marīcipas, Ajas, and Dhūmras — great sages gathered together.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ dayārthaṃ garuḍas tāṃ śākhāṃ śatayojanām jagāmādāya vegena tau cobhau gajakacchapau
english: Out of compassion for them, Garuḍa swiftly took up that branch of a hundred yojanas, together with both the elephant and the tortoise,

sanskrit: ekapādena dharmātmā bhakṣayitvā tad āmiṣam niṣādaviṣayaṃ hatvā śākhayā patagottamaḥ praharṣam atulaṃ lebhe mokṣayitvā mahāmunīn
english: And that righteous-souled best of birds, having consumed that meat with one foot, having struck the Niṣāda country with the branch, gained incomparable joy, having freed the great sages.

sanskrit: sa tenaiva praharṣeṇa dviguṇīkṛtavikramaḥ amṛtānayanārthaṃ vai cakāra matimān matim
english: And with that very joy, his power doubled, the wise one formed the resolve to fetch the ambrosia.

sanskrit: ayojālāni nirmathya bhittvā ratnagṛhaṃ varam mahendrabhavanād guptam ājahārāmṛtaṃ tataḥ
english: Having churned through the iron nets and broken open the finest jeweled chamber, he then fetched the ambrosia that was guarded in Mahendra's abode.

sanskrit: taṃ maharṣigaṇair juṣṭaṃ suparṇakṛtalakṣaṇam nāmnā subhadraṃ nyagrodhaṃ dadarśa dhanadānujaḥ
english: That banyan tree frequented by hosts of great sages, bearing the mark made by Suparṇa, named Subhadra — this the younger brother of Kubera beheld.

sanskrit: taṃ tu gatvā paraṃ pāraṃ samudrasya nadīpateḥ dadarśāśramam ekānte puṇye ramye vanāntare
english: Having gone to the far shore of the ocean, the lord of rivers, he saw a hermitage set apart in a holy, charming forest-grove.

sanskrit: tatra kṛṣṇājinadharaṃ jaṭāvalkaladhāriṇam dadarśa niyatāhāraṃ mārīcaṃ nāma rākṣasaṃ
english: There he saw the rākṣasa named Mārīca, wearing a black antelope skin, bearing matted locks and barkcloth, of regulated diet.

sanskrit: sa rāvaṇaḥ samāgamya vidhivat tena rakṣasā tataḥ paścād idaṃ vākyam abravīd vākyakovidaḥ
english: Rāvaṇa met with that rākṣasa according to proper courtesy, and thereafter, skilled in speech, spoke these words.
